title: West S
content: My mother died on April 28, 2012, at the age of 68. She had suffered from Alzheimer's dementia for the decade prior. I decided to raise money for the Alzheimer's Society charity in recognition of this. To do so, I entered my first ever half marathon race, coincidentally held on the anniversary of her death: April 28, 2013. I prepared for more than 12 months, running regularly and increasing the distance covered. On the day of the race, I felt prepared. I ran the race and found that I was running faster than ever before, likely because it was a race and I was being carried along by faster, fitter runners. At the end of the race, as I approached the finish line, I collapsed after suffering an acute hypotensive episode. I do not recall what happened, but my family told me that I was unconscious and was carried to the finish line where attempts were made to revive me: a bottle of water was poured over my head to no avail. I have seen pictures taken of me at this point, and I looked gray and lifeless. I was carried to the medical tent where a general practitioner and a paramedic treated me. I was told that my blood pressure had dropped into "double digits." I was administered a saline drip and monitored for the next hour or so, gradually reviving. The doctor told me afterward that she had been covering this race for many years and, having seen many collapses, I was the first to require a drip. I was also told that they initially considered having me airlifted to the hospital but later deemed it unnecessary. After regaining consciousness, I felt a profound sense of love. I felt unconditional love for all around me and also felt I was the recipient of that same non-judgmental love. I have no memories of seeing anything while unconscious, but I had a very strong feeling that I had been in the company of deceased loved ones. I felt equally strongly that I was meant to understand there is nothing to fear about death. This message seemed to come from my deceased loved ones, though I don't recall "hearing" it; it was just a very powerful feeling. When I came to, I also found that for the next 30 to 60 minutes my vision was extremely vivid. Colors were very striking and intense. My dad’s dirty car, which I rode home in, looked brand new, as if it had just left the showroom. The trees were the most vibrant green I have ever seen. The event was transformative for me, as I made profound changes to my life in the months that followed. I gave up drinking alcohol and have not felt the urge since. I also try hard to live meaningfully, making positive changes and offering help to others whenever possible. This is challenging, as life’s difficulties make such an outlook hard to maintain, but I have tried very hard to make concerted efforts to help people wherever I can.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: No, Collapse relating to exertion (running a half marathon), Life threatening event, but not clinical death
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: Less consciousness and alertness than normal
elements.At what time during the experience were: Just prior to collapsing and then after being revived.
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: I experienced more vibrant and vivid colors for a short period after regaining consciousness.
elements.Please compare your hearing during the e: I do not recall hearing anything during the experience.
elements.Did you encounter or become aware of any: Yes, I cannot be certain, but I believe it was probably my mother, who had died the year before.
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: I felt love, love, and more love.
elements.Have your religious practices changed si: Yes, I no longer feel like a typical 'Christian'. I feel very strongly that there is 'something' out there (whether that be 'God' or another human-applied label) as the creator of the universe and that the spirits or souls of people return to another place (from whence they came). I believe this mortal existence is a 'trial' or course we have to undergo to learn something important, probably the value of love.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was entirely consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes, I no longer fear death. I know my deceased loved ones still exist in some spiritual form and continue to take an interest in me.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, I had a very strong feeling that there is nothing to fear about death and that existence continues after physical death.
Yes, This was the overarching feeling of the experience: the importance of love, which far exceeds our understanding of it on Earth.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: I stopped drinking alcohol. I try to ensure that I do not harm other living things and am improving things for others wherever possible.
elements.Have your relationships changed specific: Yes, I try to be more genuine and loving. I tell my children about what I experienced and have used what I learned during a recent bereavement to help them through the loss of their grandad.
elements.Was the experience difficult to express: Yes, I could explain it (as I have tried to do here), but words fail to describe the impact and power of the experience I had.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience
elements.Do you have any psychic, non-ordinary or: Yes, I have noticed I occasionally have foresight. For example, someone I know will enter my mind, and a short time later I will either see them or find out my thought was correct; for instance, that they had died.
elements.Are there one or several parts of your e: The experience of love and the 'gift' of knowing that existence does not end at physical death were especially meaningful.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, In some ways, I wish I had had more experiences like this as it was so positively transformational for me.
